correctness.rationale: PASS is for repairs/1/RESULT.md, not the frozen text as written. The frozen d=3 'piecewise cubic' claim is false for lambda>0, where the branch is proportional to (sqrt(lambda^2+a^2)-lambda)^3. Also section volume is discontinuous at the horizontal cutting plane, and concentration near the maximizing plane alone would not bound the rescaled domain. The replacement proves localization before taking limits. In the critical window the unit-ball bound forces |s|=O(sqrt(eps)), and O(eps) clipping loss implies cap depth O(eps^(2/d)); the contact inequality then bounds theta by O(sqrt(eps)). At positive fixed h, work first in the ball of radius rho centered at h e_d: the near-max condition bounds z=s-h cos(theta) by O(sqrt(eps)) and clips at most eps from its equatorial halfspace. Hence z is at least a positive constant times theta and s-h=z-h(1-cos(theta)) is nonnegative and controls theta. Now the original ball's linear deficit forces both s-h and theta to be O(eps). For fixed negative h the unit-ball bound and the polar maximizing cone suffice. The rescaled indicator in each case converges off null boundaries on a bounded domain, with the full section on one side of the contact inequality and a loss bounded away from zero on the other. Integrating the correct spherical Jacobian reproduces all three constants and the crossover, including the marked wedge; the angular symmetry is exact. The normalizer is the integral of the sum of the two supports and tends to M_d,0 at zero. No coefficients or mathematical regimes were discarded.
